claims.confidence: high for deployment bottlenecks; low-medium for guarantee demand
claims.statement: EU sources identify high installation cost, complex customer journeys, installer shortages and unstable financing among heat-pump barriers; 750,000 more installers are estimated to be needed.
Preliminary 2025 data cited by the Commission shows 2.34 million new heat pumps across 13 EU countries and 11% growth, supporting a future installed base requiring performance assurance.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Homeowner, housing cooperative, installer or financing partner
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Independent pre-install prediction and post-install measured guarantee; OEMs and installers can bundle warranties
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: unknown today; proposed future ownership by the prospective business under direct guarantee contracts, subject to installer-channel terms
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Heat-pump installers, lenders, housing managers and energy auditors

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Assumption: 500-1,500 PLN per installation through installer channels
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Guarantee fee at commissioning; claims paid later from reserved funds or insurer
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unknown until loss data exists; target 35-55% after monitoring, service and risk premium
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Sensor/API integration, diagnostics, inspections and claim handling
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Insurance/legal structuring, reserves, actuarial review and consumer protection
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Commissioning fee plus annual measured-performance protection
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Monitoring, inspections, remediation contribution and claims

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Installers, OEMs, utilities and insurers add performance guarantees
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Measured seasonal performance or heating-cost outcome falls below a contractually defined weather-normalized baseline
commercial_mechanics.payer: Property owner, installer seeking sales conversion or financing partner
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Heat-pump purchase and uncertainty about realized operating cost

contrary_evidence: Performance depends on occupant behavior, weather and tariffs, complicating claims.
Risk-transfer activity may require an authorized insurer and substantial reserves.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: No guarantee book or data rights held; proposed monitoring consent, installer workflow agreement and licensed insurer contract
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Sell non-guaranteed commissioning analytics or partner with a different insurer/installer
critical_control_point.current_owner: Owners control buildings and usage data; installers/OEMs control commissioning; licensed insurers control regulated risk capacity
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: unknown today; proposed future ownership by the prospective business under direct guarantee contracts, subject to installer-channel terms
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: Parents' installer company could voluntarily support a consented pilot, but no customer data, contracts or capacity are currently granted
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business only with signed homeowner, installer and insurer agreements
critical_control_point.subject: Weather-normalized heat-pump performance guarantee and monitoring dataset

economics.acquisition_route: Start as paid commissioning analytics on 30-50 consented installs, build loss curves, then seek insurer-backed guarantee capacity
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 20,000 covered systems at 600 PLN annual net revenue yields 12m PLN revenue; at 15% EBITDA and a 5-7x specialty-services value, founder equity may exceed 5m PLN in years 9-13. Loss ratios and regulatory feasibility are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours weekly for analytics pilot; regulated product launch needs specialists and insurer operations
economics.gross_margin_basis: Fees less monitoring, channel share, servicing and risk/insurance premium
economics.payback: Analytics pilot may repay in 18-24 months; guarantee book payback unknown until loss history
economics.pricing: Assumption: 1,000-2,500 PLN commissioning analysis plus 300-900 PLN annual cover
economics.retention_or_repeat: Multi-year monitoring, renewals and installer portfolio growth

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Weather-normalized Polish installation performance and failure dataset
fingerprint.customer: Polish homeowners, housing groups and heat-pump installers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Analytics evolving into insurer-backed performance protection
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Owner or channel pays at commissioning; claim event is underperformance
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Electrified heating scales faster than trusted installation outcomes

founder_fit: Renewable installation and quantitative modeling fit.
A consented analytics pilot is capital-feasible.
Regulated risk transfer exceeds solo-founder competence and requires partners.
thesis: Future state: heat-pump buyers purchase a measured outcome, not just equipment. The missing financial mechanism is an insurer-backed, weather-normalized performance guarantee grounded in commissioning and operating data.
title: Heat-Pump Performance Guarantee
